text: ok so that being said you did say the literal word port. so what does that word mean and is that a port or what? if i port something but change the behavior of it, is it still a port or is it just something else
resolution: Answered the definitional question: a port means moving code to a new substrate while PRESERVING behavior — parity is the contract. The native solidify (framework/gpu/3d.zig meshSolidifySelection) ported the geometry faithfully but changed observable behavior (old studio: inner cap + each rim wall individually selectable; native: whole slab inherits one group id and picks as one face). Verdict given to the user: that makes it a port with a parity regression, not a sanctioned redesign — the one-face behavior was never ruled, so it's a bug against the reference, and the fix (mint fresh group ids for inner cap + rim walls) is owed. No code changed this req; awaiting the user's go to restore parity.
